title: Build a content repurposing pipeline
description: A system that turns one long-form post into ready-to-ship versions for every channel you use.

pull.title: Pull
pull.content: Downloading the latest changes from GitHub to your computer so your local copy is up to date. Claude pulls before starting work to make sure it's building on the newest version, not an old one.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

slack.title: Slack
slack.content: The team messaging app most companies run on. In Level 2, students connect Slack to their AI tools to trigger workflows from messages, post AI-generated updates to channels, or summarize threads automatically.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

script.title: Script
script.content: A small piece of code that tells a computer how to complete a task automatically — rename these files, pull this data, send that report. Scripts are deterministic: same input, same result, no model call needed. Claude writes them; you don't have to.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.content: A multi-step process Claude runs to accomplish a goal — for example: read emails → filter by topic → summarize → post to Slack. Workflows can be run manually or on a schedule.

anthropic.title: Anthropic
anthropic.content: The company that created Claude. An AI safety company focused on building reliable, interpretable AI systems.

voice-guide.title: Voice Guide
voice-guide.content: A file that captures how you write — your tone, vocabulary, sentence structure, and preferences. Share it with Claude so it writes in your style instead of generic AI voice.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

children.text: One published post rarely does the work by itself. This system reads a long-form source, a blog post, a webinar recording, a podcast episode, and turns it into channel-native derivatives, a LinkedIn post, an email blurb, ad copy, a short-form video script, each matched to its channel's format instead of one message pasted everywhere. [Anthropic](#tooltip-anthropic)'s own growth marketing team cut ad creation time from 30 minutes to 30 seconds per ad running this kind of [workflow](#tooltip-workflow), per [Anthropic's account of how its marketing team uses Claude](https://claude.com/blog/how-anthropic-uses-claude-marketing).

86% of B2B marketing teams now use AI for content generation, but only 64% say that content drives meaningful results, per the [Content Marketing Institute's B2B Content Marketing Benchmarks 2026](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/research/b2b-research). The gap is volume without a system to make each derivative good. One well-built source asset can outproduce a content calendar built post by post.

Run it as a paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) every time you publish, a saved [skill](#tooltip-skill), or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that watches your CMS for new posts. Every version routes derivatives to a review queue before anything goes out under your name.
Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming your source content, your channels, your voice, and your review step.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that turns one piece of long-form content I publish into ready-to-post derivatives for the other channels I use. Ask me questions, one at a time, about what my source content usually is, which channels I actually post to and how often, what makes a post on each channel good versus generic, and how I want to review derivatives before they go out. Then write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview surfaces decisions you didn't know you needed to make, and the scope document becomes the brief for every build session after it.

items: Where the source content lives (a CMS, a shared drive, a podcast host) before automating the [pull](#tooltip-pull).
Whether derivatives get scheduled directly or land in a review queue first.
How many channels launch in v1. One well-tuned derivative beats five mediocre ones.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first by pasting it into a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model) and asking it to poke holes. Then gather any access it calls for. Common [connectors](#tooltip-tool-connectors) are your CMS or blog platform (WordPress, Webflow, Ghost), a scheduling tool (Buffer, Hootsuite, native platform scheduling), and a review surface ([Slack](#tooltip-slack), email, a shared doc). The paste-in version needs none.
**Create.** Build your system and test it on a real source asset. The prompt below is an example. Your scope document gives a version for your setup.

children.prompt:
Goal: Turn [the source asset, e.g., this blog post or transcript] into a ready-to-post derivative for [channel, e.g., LinkedIn].

Context: Our brand voice is [2-3 adjectives, e.g., direct, a little irreverent, no corporate softening]. This channel's format is [length, tone, and structure norms for that channel]. Past examples of posts that worked are [paste 1-2].

Rules:
- Do not invent statistics, quotes, or claims not in the source.
- Flag anything you are unsure how to phrase instead of guessing.
- Keep it under [word/character limit].

Output format: the finished post, plus a one-line note on what you changed from the source and why.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: naming the exact voice and channel norms up front stops the derivative from reading like a generic paste of the source.

children.text: **Review.** Check the output against your scope. Voice on target, nothing invented, format fits the channel?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what went wrong ("too long for this channel" or "that line invents a stat") and fold each correction into the rules.

items: Add a style-check pass against your brand [voice guide](#tooltip-voice-guide) before anything ships.
Auto-generate three headline variants per derivative.
Track which derivative types get real engagement and drop the ones that don't.
Extend to video [scripts](#tooltip-script) once the b-roll or editor pipeline exists.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat draft rubric and run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each derivative, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for date, source asset, channel, revisions needed before it shipped, and what rule I changed. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the judgment call, and the log columns make a drifting voice visible after a handful of derivatives.

children.text: **Log** every run against the rubric. Note the date, which rubric checks passed or failed, and what you changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the system passes the rubric a few runs straight, package the prompt and your corrected rules into a reusable AI skill. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s built-in skill-creator skill will interview you and write the skill for you, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).
A pipeline that runs unattended drifts from your voice long before you notice. Review the first ten outputs closely, not just the first one.
